Each triangle's three edges stay inside its team, 3 in each diagonal cell, and the single cross edge C–D (accent) puts 1 in each off-diagonal cell." width="100%"} Entry `[i][j]` adds up a value over the edges from the `i`-th row's nodes to the `j`-th column's nodes. With `node_attr=None` the rows and columns are the nodes themselves, so this is an adjacency matrix holding any edge attribute; with `node_attr=` they are the values of a node attribute, so the matrix tallies the edges (or their weights) between groups of nodes, such as how many ties run within and between departments. Each edge adds its `edge_attr=` value (`1` by default, so entries count edges). On an undirected graph the matrix is symmetric: each edge adds to both of its cells, a self-loop or an edge within one group to its diagonal cell once. Matches NetworkX's `attr_matrix()`. NetworkX returns only the matrix when `rc_order=` is given, and otherwise orders the rows arbitrarily; EdgeCase always returns the matrix together with its row labels, sorted unless `rc_order=` fixes them. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[str, Callable[[rust.Edge], float], None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : What each edge adds. If `None` (default), `1`. `"weight"` adds the edge weight (`1` for an edge without one); any other string names an edge attribute, which every edge must have. A function is called with each `Edge` and returns its value. [node_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[str, Callable[[rust.Node], Any], None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : What labels the rows and columns. If `None` (default), the node IDs. A string names a node attribute, which every node must have; a function is called with each `Node` and returns its value. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, divide each row by its sum, so that row `i` gives the fraction of the `i`-th row's edge value that goes to each column. Rows that sum to zero stay zero (NetworkX gives NaN). Default is `False`. [rc_order]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[list]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The row and column labels, in order: node IDs or labels when `node_attr=` is `None`, attribute values otherwise. Edges with an endpoint whose label isn't listed are left out. If `None` (default), every label is used, sorted (by its text if the labels can't be compared). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[list[float]], list]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(matrix, labels)`: the square matrix as a list of rows, and the node IDs or attribute values labelling its rows and columns. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node or edge lacks the named attribute, an edge's value isn't a number, or `rc_order=` lists a label twice. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Count the ties within and between two teams, and the share of each team's ties that stay inside it: ::: {#79d65d87 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("A", "C")]) ) graph.set_node_attrs("team", {1: "red", 2: "red", 3: "blue", 4: "blue"}) graph.attr_matrix(node_attr="team", rc_order=["red", "blue"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ([[1.0, 2.0], [2.0, 1.0]], ['red', 'blue']) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#0c3bf1fc .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.attr_matrix(node_attr="team", rc_order=["red", "blue"], normalized=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ([[0.3333333333333333, 0.6666666666666666], [0.6666666666666666, 0.3333333333333333]], ['red', 'blue']) ``` ::: :::
